- Connectors describe memberships but converge through `buildAccessGraph`; none supplies purpose directly.

So accidental arming while old pods live: no, absent privileged manual SQL or a future caller of the optional helper argument.

End-to-end rollout safety: no, because the inert interval permits new/repointed caller edges that A2 would later bless, and in-flight schema operations can straddle the backfill.

## B. Complete relationship-write inventory

Every SQL write is covered by the database trigger once classified. Additional protection is:

| Write path | Protection |
|---|---|
| `upsertEdges` INSERT/UPSERT | Trigger only; ACL callers pass a flagged transaction ([edge-writes.ts:103-127](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/utils/edge-writes.ts:103)) |
| Access-graph departure UPDATE | Trigger + `withAclEdgeWrite` flag ([access-graph.ts:536-577](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/authz/access-graph.ts:536)) |
| GitHub team-graph INSERT | Trigger + `withAclEdgeWrite` flag ([github-team-graph.ts:291-310](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/gateway/routes/public/github-team-graph.ts:291)) |
| `manage_entity link` INSERT | Call-site classification check + trigger ([manage_entity.ts:1576-1600](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity.ts:1576)) |
| `unlink` soft-delete | Shared call-site check + trigger ([manage_entity.ts:1519-1551](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity.ts:1519)) |
| `update_link` UPDATE | Same call-site check + trigger |
| Two channel-about tombstones | Trigger only; normally an unclassified `about` type ([channel-about.ts:361-383](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/authz/channel-about.ts:361), [channel-about.ts:428-449](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/authz/channel-about.ts:428)) |
| `force_delete_tree` hard DELETE | Trigger under deliberate `withAclPrivilege` ([entity-management.ts:1344-1359](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/utils/entity-management.ts:1344)) |
| Merge authorization tombstone | Trigger under deliberate privilege |
| Merge collision tombstone | Trigger only |
| Merge endpoint repoint | Trigger only |
| Unmerge ledger restore | Trigger only |

Once A2 is settled, normal link/unlink/update callers cannot directly mint/revoke. However:

- Merge and force-delete remain caller-triggerable, deliberately privileged revocation paths.
- The OLD-type UPDATE hole above bypasses the trigger.
- Type/rule mutations are not covered by this trigger at all. They rely only on application checks in `requireRelationshipType`, `remove_rule`, and inverse resolution ([manage_entity_schema.ts:861-919](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity_schema.ts:861), [manage_entity_schema.ts:1344-1382](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity_schema.ts:1344)). Those checks and writes are separate autocommits, so a request that reads `purpose=NULL` immediately before A2 can mutate the type/rules after the backfill commits.

## C. `withAclPrivilege`

For current non-nested uses, yes: enforcement is restored mid-transaction. It sets transaction-local `on`, executes the callback, and explicitly sets `off` in `finally` ([relationship-validation.ts:92-98](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/utils/relationship-validation.ts:92)).

PostgreSQL subtransaction behavior is compatible:

- Releasing a savepoint preserves its final local setting, which is why explicit `off` matters.
- Rolling back a savepoint removes SET LOCAL changes made after it.
- A database error that leaves the transaction aborted also prevents subsequent writes; rollback removes the local setting.

Caveat: it does not restore the prior value; it forces `off`. Nested `withAclPrivilege` calls would disable an outer privileged section prematurely. That is fail-closed, but the helper is not composable. `withAclEdgeWrite` now rejects an already-open postgres.js transaction and also explicitly resets through `withAclPrivilege` ([relationship-validation.ts:60-73](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/utils/relationship-validation.ts:60)).

## D. Ledger

Exclusion is correct for pre-merge authorization edges; restoring them would resurrect stale grants and hit the trigger. It intentionally narrows the header’s “restore relationship endpoints” exactness promise ([entity-merge.ts:20-24](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/utils/entity-merge.ts:20)) to ordinary relationships.

It should not break an immediate unmerge containing mixed ordinary/auth edges. It is incomplete for post-merge ACL changes, especially sync→unmerge, as described above. That needs explicit fail-closed invalidation/reconciliation rather than ledger restoration.

## E. Locks and JOIN

`FOR UPDATE OF r` is correct for the steady-state query: it locks only relationship rows, in `r.id` order, and does not introduce a new type-row lock order. I do not see a new conventional deadlock cycle.

There is a classification race because `rt` is not locked or revalidated:

- Merge’s first statement can see `purpose=NULL` and include the edge in the ledger.
- A2 can then commit `purpose='authorization'`.
- A later merge statement sees the new classification and tombstones the edge.
- The ledger still contains it, so unmerge later attempts an unprivileged restore and is rejected.

Alternatively, if merge finishes first, it can repoint the unclassified grant and A2 then classifies the transferred result. The mutable JOIN predicate at [entity-merge.ts:237-251](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/utils/entity-merge.ts:237) therefore has an activation-time correctness problem even though its row-lock syntax is valid.

## F. Missing security tests

At minimum:

- UPDATE changing `relationship_type_id` away from, into, and between authorization types.
- A1 caller-minted `member_of` followed by simulated A2 backfill.
- Concurrent classification versus link/unlink, schema update/delete/rules/inverse, and merge.
- Mixed ordinary + authorization merge/unmerge, including collisions.
- Merge → real `buildAccessGraph` sync → unmerge, proving no stale winner grant.
- Actual `force_delete_tree`; the current test performs raw DELETE despite claiming to exercise that surface ([acl-edge-chokepoint.test.ts:120-126](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/__tests__/integration/authz/acl-edge-chokepoint.test.ts:120)).
- Actual classified `buildAccessGraph` and GitHub team-graph paths; current production graph tests leave the type unclassified.
- `withAclPrivilege` on JS failure, SQL failure, real savepoint rollback/release, and nested helper calls.
- Every schema action: update, delete/archive, add_rule, remove_rule, both inverse create/update paths. Current tests cover delete, remove_rule, and inverse-create, but not the full matrix.
- Migration-level assertion that deploy 1 leaves every production-created type unclassified.
- Ensure the trigger-cost test restores the trigger in `finally`; it currently drops/recreates without failure-safe cleanup ([acl-trigger-cost.test.ts:82-91](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/__tests__/integration/authz/acl-trigger-cost.test.ts:82)).

**VERDICT: NOT SAFE — confidence 95/100.**
